Each Red host and its assigned inner also declare the same parsed Red subnet.
entries.title: One inner component per Red network

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Lean checks distinct declared trust domains and their sampled public CA identifiers. Each local and declared peer identity is bound to the observed certificate inventory, including issuer and authority-key metadata. Equal trust domains agree on sampled CA identities; different trust domains have distinct reported CA key identifiers. The checks do not prove signature validity, private-key independence, absence of cross-signing, exhaustive credential stores, or actual rejection of unauthorized peers. Management infrastructure is optional and excluded; MACsec CAK clauses are inactive.
entries.model_claim: The retained inner security levels use distinct declared trust labels and distinct sampled public CA key identifiers. Complete local/peer/CA inventories bind those observations to all eight declared encryptor endpoints. Matching sampled metadata is a bounded observation claim, not a cryptographic validation result.
entries.title: Cryptographic security-level separation

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The flow theorems reject cross-level transmission and delivery for every modeled state and packet, and permit authorized same-level delivery under readiness assumptions. They do not promise unconditional delivery during failures, infer real identities from packet addresses, or prove computational secrecy. Shared infrastructure is allowed by this architectural statement, although separate physical-component requirements still apply elsewhere.
entries.model_claim: Cross-level and unauthorized modeled traffic is blocked for every readiness state. An authorized same-level packet transmits and is delivered when the specified sender/receiver readiness assumptions hold. The latter is a conditional model result, not unconditional network availability.
entries.title: No inter-level Red communication

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Lean proves that every nonempty declared Gray interface address parses and that all numeric Gray addresses are distinct across interfaces, sites, and levels. The stronger global uniqueness check covers the address-assignment clause. Outer selectors are also tied to the declared inner peer endpoints, and forwarding contracts restrict the modeled FORWARD subset. Address attribution, complete packet-class/control exceptions, and Linux fidelity remain separate obligations.
entries.model_claim: The imported addressed Gray interfaces have valid, globally distinct numeric IPv4 addresses. Tunnel-derived outer selectors bind the intended inner peers, and accepted modeled outer traffic satisfies the corresponding address/direction/protocol contract.
entries.title: Gray address assignment and intended peers

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The Gray cut proof establishes that all imported virtual Gray walks between differently labeled inner components encounter a removed Gray Firewall. It covers arbitrary finite path lengths. Physical realization and graph completeness remain premises; the source does not impose a same-level firewall waypoint.
entries.model_claim: Every imported Gray path joining differently labeled inner components includes a Gray Firewall, as established by removing those firewalls and proving no bypass walk remains. The induction covers all finite walks. Same-level paths need no universal waypoint under this statement.
entries.title: All cross-level Gray paths are filtered

entries.disposition: Conditional service branch not exercised in the selected projection
entries.reason: The AW grouping and filtering clauses are outside the experiment. No online local Gray CA service is declared in the projection, so its conditional grouping is not exercised. Loaded trust anchors do not establish a hosted CA service. Introducing a local CA would require an authoritative classification ordering and path analysis; absent AWs create no gap now.
entries.title: Gray management grouped with highest level

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Imported outer FORWARD tables have their own policy guards independently of the Gray Firewalls, and modeled unauthorized/cross-level Red flows are blocked. Those facts support an additional outer enforcement layer. Full outer interface filtering, approved control/service exceptions, and real peer authentication still need explicit semantics and evidence.
entries.model_claim: The imported outer encryptors have their own guarded FORWARD tables, and the symbolic authorization relation blocks cross-level and unauthorized Red transmission. The existence of Gray Firewalls is not used as a substitute for those outer rules. Complete outer interface filtering remains outside the checked contribution.
entries.title: Outer filtering is additional to Gray firewalls

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The untrusted-Black placement and bounded FORWARD policy now have proofs. Shared-host containers do not establish physical separation, no product listing is supplied, and INPUT/OUTPUT plus the complete approved control set remain outside the model. SR-12 retains its narrower Public Internet trigger.
entries.model_claim: Removing Outer Firewall vertices from the retained Red/Gray/Black cable graph disconnects every outer encryptor from BLACK for all finite walks. Each outer also has a checked two-edge path through an Outer Firewall in the original graph, so the cut does not rely on disconnection. The bounded FORWARD allowlist is checked at every Outer Firewall.
entries.title: Untrusted Black requires Outer Firewall in prose

entries.reason: The supplied prose makes Public Internet the TRANSEC trigger, while OR-9 is an Objective with a narrower MACsec condition. Node-1's simulated Black network is not identified as the Public Internet. A selected Internet design needs an authoritative resolution; the table must not silently erase the prose or make TRANSEC universally mandatory.
entries.title: Outer TRANSEC in prose

entries.reason: The export does not establish ownership/control, trusted-third-party status, or facility protection at the highest connected classification. It also does not assign a highest classification to S1/S2. The stated exception for the Outer Firewall must be retained when obtaining the required physical evidence.
entries.title: Gray ownership and physical protection

entries.reason: No classification authority has determined whether Gray metadata is itself classified. The applicability limitation concerns that additional Gray information, not the intended singly encrypted Red payload. A determination about Gray addresses and other metadata is required; the model cannot invent one.
entries.title: Gray information-classification limitation

entries.reason: Node-1 selects the permitted IPsec/IPsec combination. The other three combinations are alternatives, not missing mandatory features. Outer-MACsec point-to-point constraints would apply only to a newly selected MACsec profile; the current Lean proofs do not establish those unimplemented alternatives.
entries.title: Allowed protocol layering

entries.reason: No inner MACsec layer or MACsec-over-IP path is selected. The encapsulation obligation is therefore inactive for the pinned profile. Adding MACsec requires end-to-end frame-protection semantics and resolution of the standalone encapsulator boundary described in ISSUE-07.
entries.title: MACsec must retain end-to-end inner protection

entries.reason: The profile does not select MACsec encapsulation, clear VLAN tags, or XPN. The inventory grants options and does not require deploying each feature. A future choice would need AO approval where specified and must preserve SR-10's separate physical-interface restriction.
entries.title: MACsec encapsulation options and optional features

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The symbolic flow requires independent inner and outer peer-authenticated flags and blocks transmission when either flag is false. Intended configurations select public-key authentication at both IPsec layers. The theorem assumes the flags correctly summarize IKE, certificate, and trust checks; it does not prove those checks or the unselected MACsec handshake.
entries.model_claim: Transmission fails if either peer-authentication flag is false. The proof therefore keeps the two modeled authentication dependencies separate. It assumes the flags faithfully represent actual certificate authentication and does not prove an IKE or MACsec handshake.
entries.title: Mutual device authentication

entries.reason: Observed certificate subjects identify devices, but that evidence does not establish every Non-Person Entity certificate and lifecycle requirement in the missing annexes. The NSA-approved KGS condition applies to selected CAK/CKN generation, which is absent here. A complete IPsec certificate policy and annex-based credential audit are still required.
entries.title: Device certificates and symmetric-key generation

entries.reason: The selected profile does not add RFC 8784 preshared-key augmentation. Its absence does not violate a permission, and a PSK-only replacement would not satisfy the separate required certificate authentication. Selecting the augmentation would require the Symmetric Key Management Annex and matching IKE evidence.
entries.title: Optional IPsec preshared-key augmentation

entries.reason: The profile consistently uses IPv4, which is allowed by the independent address-family choices. The permission does not require simultaneous IPv4 and IPv6 support. No IPv6 implementation theorem is claimed by the current IPv4 model.
entries.title: IPv4/IPv6 independence

entries.reason: The snapshot contains specific control allowances, including Black underlay OSPF on routers and IKE on gateways. The organization/AO-approved control policy is missing, and the model does not cover all local control traffic or multicast handling. A proof must retain necessary Layer 2 control and explicit approvals rather than treat every non-data packet as forbidden.
entries.title: Control-plane policy

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The outer data model requires an outer policy and encryption step; the imported FORWARD tables reject untagged packets. Static routes are declared on outer encryptors, while OSPF belongs to BLACK and the separate Outer Firewalls. The no-routing-protocol clause and full real Gray-to-Black coverage still require process/interface semantics beyond the existing data-path theorem.
entries.model_claim: Untagged outer forwarding is rejected, and successful symbolic protected-data transmission includes outer encryption with policy readiness. The no-routing-protocol clause is not proved by those theorems. OSPF on separate Black/Outer Firewall routers is not an outer-encryptor protocol.
entries.title: Outer routing restriction and encrypted forwarding

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The modeled transmit and delivery operations include inner encryption/decryption and reject untagged encryptor forwarding. The approved Red service addresses and ports are not supplied, and the model does not prove full service-specific filtering. An explicit service policy and complete ingress/egress model are needed for the rest of the statement.
entries.model_claim: The symbolic data path includes inner encryption before transmission and inner decryption before delivery, while imported encryptor tables reject untagged forwarding. The theorem does not supply the missing organization-approved Red service address/port policy.
entries.title: Inner Red-side service restriction

entries.reason: Physical and cryptographic separation of management traffic from data is outside the experiment because management traffic is absent by assumption. Necessary control traffic remains subject to its own retained requirements. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Data/management traffic separation

entries.reason: Red-versus-Gray administrator access restrictions concern omitted workstations and sessions. The data-path claims do not depend on the full snapshot management graph. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Separate administration domains

entries.reason: The inventory explicitly requires Red and Gray AWs in a complete MSC solution. The research experiment deliberately excludes that requirement along with the workstations. The exclusion limits the experiment scope and does not reinterpret the source as making AWs optional. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Mandatory administrative workstations

entries.reason: Gray management attachment and directional management ACLs concern omitted management links, services, and traffic. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Gray management attachment and directional ACLs

entries.reason: Protection of management sessions, including any double protection over Black, concerns traffic excluded from the experiment. The separate protected-Red-data encryption claim remains in scope. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Protected management sessions

entries.reason: Independent-versus-central administration is outside the experiment because no management workflow is selected. The assessment makes no compliance claim for either administration alternative. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Choice of independent or central management

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The retained contribution concerns symmetric peer declarations and sampled IPsec establishment. Administrative independence, management transit over Black, and authentication-service attachment are outside the experiment. The assessment does not claim that the full independent-management architecture is established. The remaining retained trust questions concern actual CA relationships and signing/revocation information for the data tunnels; MACsec CAK conditions are inactive.
entries.model_claim: Declared tunnel endpoints have matching reverse peers, selectors, and trust data, and the saved encryptor observations report establishment. Those retained facts support peer interoperability during collection. No management-network or administrative-independence claim is included.
entries.title: Independently managed sites

entries.reason: Central-site management personnel and the central-management service architecture are outside the experiment. Trust separation of the retained data tunnels is assessed separately under the applicable tunnel and trust entries. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Central-management trust and authentication

entries.reason: Enterprise Gray central-management transport and inter-site management encryption are outside the experiment. Their absence supplies no counterexample to protected Red-data double encryption. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Central-management transport

entries.reason: The snapshot begins after provisioning and records neither physical-area security nor authorization of the provisioning personnel. Successful deployment does not prove that initial setup occurred out of band under the required protections. Dated provisioning and access records are necessary. The remaining question concerns provisioning or human authorization independently of any AW container; it is not an extra premise of the protected-data theorem.
entries.title: Protected out-of-band provisioning

entries.reason: Loaded device certificates and trust anchors support the result of provisioning, but do not establish component-local key generation, CSR origin, or authorized administrator actions. The export deliberately omits private keys and is not a provisioning audit trail. The selected certificate workflow needs lifecycle evidence; the approved KGS clause remains conditional on MACsec PSK use. The remaining question concerns provisioning or human authorization independently of any AW container; it is not an extra premise of the protected-data theorem.
entries.title: Certificate and CAK provisioning procedure

entries.reason: AW host dedication, prohibited co-hosting, patching, and power state concern omitted workstations and hosts. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Dedicated AW hosts and workstations

entries.reason: No Gray SIEM is declared, and the source explicitly makes the component optional. Its absence is not an unmet mandatory SIEM deployment requirement. If selected, its alert/log behavior needs a model; the separate Continuous Monitoring Annex obligations remain unresolved regardless of that choice.
entries.title: Gray SIEM is optional, monitoring is not waived

entries.reason: No Red SIEM is declared in node-1. The described collection, alerting, and recommended encrypted transport cannot be proved for an absent component and should not be converted into an unconditional requirement to add one. A selected SIEM would require log-source and alert-policy evidence.
entries.title: Red SIEM behavior

entries.reason: The standalone MSC profile does not declare an Inner Firewall. The inventory explicitly says MSC alone does not require that device, so absence is not a violation. Any integrated CP that changes the condition must be assessed separately.
entries.title: Inner Firewall is not required by MSC alone

entries.reason: Node-1 does not provide a proved high-availability or bounded-failover guarantee. The CP makes automatic high availability a non-goal and permits qualifying parallel redundancy. Transport-readiness assumptions in the Lean model must not be presented as a new CP liveness requirement or as proof of redundancy.
entries.title: Availability and redundant components

entries.reason: The deployed classical IKEv2 proposal does not implement the stated CNSA 2.0 intermediate ML-KEM exchange and ML-DSA authentication sequence. The Objective is therefore not established. The initial CNSA 1.0 exchange and named standards must remain as specified in the supplied version rather than being replaced with a different current profile.
entries.title: CNSA 2.0 IPsec exchange sequencing

entries.reason: Neither MACsec EAP-TLS nor its CNSA 2.0 Objective branch is selected. No TLS 1.3, ML-KEM-1024, or ML-DSA-87 handshake evidence exists for that branch. An IPsec tunnel using AES-GCM cannot prove the separate EAP-TLS conditions.
entries.title: CNSA 2.0 MACsec EAP-TLS

entries.reason: No software/firmware signing chain using LMS, XMSS, or ML-DSA-87 is supplied. The Objective allows one of those algorithms, so requiring all three would be a misinterpretation. Signature provenance and verification evidence are needed for the selected alternative.
entries.title: Software/firmware signing objective

entries.reason: No NIAP evaluation baseline or PMO/NIAP statement for modified components is supplied. The emulator cannot infer certification continuity from functioning modified code. The condition requires component-specific assurance evidence when an evaluated component is modified.
entries.title: NIAP component modification

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: Sampled established tunnels and passing probes provide limited interoperability evidence for the selected peers. They establish neither NIAP certification nor CSfC listing, and neither approval alone would imply interoperability. A complete assessment needs product-list evidence and the required interoperability test scope. Excluded management probe outcomes do not serve as premises of the retained data-path theorems. The full probe report and management observations are optional diagnostics and cannot block the retained MSC proof review.
entries.model_claim: All retained encryptor observations report matching established sessions during the snapshot interval. The sampled result does not establish product approval or future interoperability.
entries.title: Component-list assurance and interoperability

entries.reason: No complete applicable CNSS/local-policy set, conflict-report history, or Top Secret approval is supplied. S1/S2 are not assigned Secret or Top Secret by the model. The policy and classification decisions must precede compliance checks, with CP precedence retained where the source specifies it.
entries.title: Other policy and Top Secret scope

entries.reason: The model has no incident-classification process or records distinguishing explained benign events from unexplained activity. The reporting definition must presume unexplained activity malicious until a known non-malicious explanation is established. A formal workflow could encode that rule, but the current packet model does not show it is followed.
entries.title: Definition of malicious for reporting

entries.reason: No complete record establishes Security Administrator monitoring, patching, incident reporting, integration, escort, or auxiliary-device duties. Device configuration proves none of those human actions. Role assignments and dated operational evidence are needed while preserving incompatible-role restrictions.
entries.title: Security Administrator duties

entries.reason: The snapshot has no auditor identity, action history, System Audit Capability Survey, or complete access-control policy. A network baseline may support an audit, but does not prove the auditor duties or access limits. Separate human role and audit-workflow evidence are required.
entries.title: Auditor duties and access

entries.reason: No external Integrator arrangement is identified, and employing one is optional. The customer's optional development staffing restriction must not become a universal mandate. Mandatory operational administrator separation remains governed separately by RB-5.
entries.title: Optional external Integrator

entries.reason: No customer authorization package, AO decisions, annual-audit records, control approvals, or NSA variant approval is included. The model can support the technical evidence in an approval process but cannot establish those decisions. Each required organizational action needs an authoritative record.
entries.title: AO and customer approval responsibilities

entries.disposition: Checked model contribution; full statement not established
entries.reason: The snapshot preserves a logical configuration baseline and the probe theorem checks that the recorded report passed 273 checks. The mandatory Testing Annex and local AO test requirements are absent, and no Final Test Report submission is evidenced. Whole-solution testing and required baseline fields remain unproved; the two-person testing approach is a recommendation rather than an invented mandate. Excluded management probe outcomes do not serve as premises of the retained data-path theorems. The full probe report and management observations are optional diagnostics and cannot block the retained MSC proof review.
entries.model_claim: The retained baseline has unique device IDs and valid cable endpoints. Retained devices report running state, no collection errors, and the expected specification hash. Optional management devices and their probe outcomes are excluded from required acceptance.
entries.title: Testing method and evidence

entries.reason: The NSA MSC Risk Assessment and evidence of AO receipt are absent. The topology does not define the complete threat/failure model and cannot stand in for the assessment. Obtain the assessment and receipt evidence before claiming that approval prerequisite.
entries.title: Risk-assessment dependency

entries.reason: No NSA registration, approval date, annual renewal, or change-update record is supplied. The six-month new-version deadline also differs from GD-11's next-renewal wording. Both statements are preserved until an authoritative interpretation and dated registration history permit a timing check.
entries.title: Registration and update timing

entries.reason: BLACK provides transport routing, but the source does not require an optional screening router. Such a Black-side router cannot silently substitute for a required separate, listed Outer Firewall. The optional arrangement creates no missing-device failure for the selected profile.
entries.title: Optional screening router

entries.reason: The pinned instance has two sites and two levels, so its concrete proofs do not establish every possible scale. The CP's absence of a design count limit is a permission, not a throughput or universal implementation theorem. No additional unclassified enclave is declared; adding one activates its own inner-component obligation, and outer-MACsec designs retain the point-to-point limit.
entries.title: Scalability and unclassified enclave option

entries.reason: The snapshot resolves device identity with O_A1, O_A2, O_B1, and O_B2. Those distinct IDs identify four logical encryptors and must not be interpreted as four physical appliances or a redundancy guarantee. Hardware separation and failover remain separate claims.
entries.title: Repeated outer-component labels in the example

entries.reason: Node-1 adds four Outer Firewalls omitted from the example image. The design therefore addresses the virtual placement omission, but not physical separation or product approval. The broader untrusted-Black prose remains relevant even though SR-12 explicitly names Public Internet.
entries.title: Untrusted Black and omitted Outer Firewalls

entries.reason: The supplied Section 5.2 wording conflicts with the same-level communication permitted elsewhere. Node-1 follows the explicit same-level peer rules and cross-level isolation interpretation. That implementation choice is recorded as an interpretation, not an authoritative correction of the PDF.
entries.title: Section 5.2 says to block same-security-level inner peers

entries.reason: The source difference between physical/cryptographic separation and minimum logical management/data separation is preserved for a future management assessment. Neither formulation is a proof obligation in the selected experiment. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Physical/cryptographic separation versus minimum logical separation

entries.reason: The IPsec lab does not identify simulated Black as Public Internet. The prose and OR-9 nevertheless retain different TRANSEC triggers and modalities for future applicable designs. The review does not silently label TRANSEC universally optional or mandatory.
entries.title: TRANSEC requirement strength and trigger differ

entries.reason: The pinned evidence has no registration timeline with which to evaluate either deadline. GD-11 and Section 13.3 are retained separately. A formal deadline predicate needs an authoritative resolution rather than choosing the easier date.
entries.title: New-version compliance deadline

entries.reason: No standalone inner-MACsec encapsulator exists in node-1. The source-boundary conflict is therefore dormant for the current profile, not resolved by it. A MACsec extension must explicitly determine which Solution Component obligations apply to the encapsulator.
entries.title: Standalone inner-MACsec encapsulator boundary

entries.reason: The assessment preserves OR-9/PF-10 as Objective rows with blank alternatives and MD-3/MD-14 as Threshold alternatives. Those metadata facts can be checked against the PDF. They are source annotations rather than network behavior to prove.
entries.title: Objective rows with blank alternative cells; MACsec T/T alternatives

entries.reason: The retained filter interpretation keeps peer data, applicable revocation, and control exceptions distinct. Management exceptions are outside the experiment. A peer allowlist alone still cannot establish required service availability, and deny-all cannot establish a positive allowance. The remaining packet-class policy and precedence questions do not depend on AWs.
entries.title: Peer-only filtering and explicit service exceptions

entries.reason: The Gray-AW initiation wording and its Red-AW context concern management traffic omitted from the experiment. The source issue does not affect retained data or control claims. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: Unqualified Gray-AW initiation wording

entries.reason: The protected-data model proves nested processing for its packet type. OR-4 retains its explicit control exception and the applicable PF-3/PF-4 control allowances. Management traffic is excluded and contributes no gap or counterexample. The remaining question is coverage of retained non-control data and refinement to actual packet processing, not a demand that every Black packet be encrypted twice.
entries.title: No-bypass and allowed control-plane traffic

entries.reason: The dated snapshot adds concrete addresses, interfaces, rules, peer declarations, and sampled runtime facts to the diagram. Its evidence supports only the modeled properties and does not supply physical assurance, approvals, complete policy, or classification ordering. Those missing facts must remain explicit inputs.
entries.title: Diagram is connectivity, not evidence of policy

entries.reason: The available tests and proofs cover a selected network model, not the absent annexes or unspecified quantitative guarantees. No unconditional delivery, general loop-freedom, or formal noninterference requirement is manufactured from the image. Additional specifications are prerequisites for those distinct claims.
entries.title: No supplied comprehensive annex requirements or quantitative liveness spec

entries.reason: The Key Management Requirements Annex is not supplied, so relocated key-management obligations and complete credential lifecycle conditions cannot be reconstructed soundly. Loaded certificates/CRLs support only the observed configuration. Obtain the annex and map its applicable rows before claiming full key-management compliance.
entries.title: CSfC Key Management Requirements Annex

entries.reason: The selected IPsec profile does not use MACsec CAKs or RFC 8784 PSK augmentation. If symmetric-key features are selected, the missing Symmetric Key Management Annex becomes necessary to assess generation, handling, and destruction. entries.reason: A short snapshot and probe report do not establish continuous monitoring. The missing annex defines the relocated monitoring/auditing requirements and must be obtained. No SIEM deployment choice waives applicable monitoring obligations.
entries.title: CSfC Continuous Monitoring Annex

entries.reason: The Enterprise Gray Annex is a dependency of the excluded central-management architecture. Its absence does not block the retained data-path assessment. The source entry remains recorded, but it is neither a failure nor a proved obligation in this assessment.
entries.title: CSfC Enterprise Gray Implementation Requirements Annex

entries.reason: TR-1 explicitly depends on the missing Testing Annex. The 273 emulator checks cannot establish completeness against tests whose requirements are unavailable. Obtain the annex and produce a per-test evidence mapping.
entries.title: CSfC MSC CP Testing Annex

entries.reason: The missing NSA MSC Risk Assessment is an AO approval input. The model's chosen failure flags do not reconstruct the assessment or prove that the AO considered it. Obtain both the assessment and the applicable receipt/review evidence.
entries.title: NSA MSC Risk Assessment

Such policy choices cannot be inferred from whichever traffic the emulator happens to allow. They must be supplied as explicit evidence and checked separately from implementation behavior.
entries.title: AO/organizational policy and local implementation
